body.prose:
A relation is held by the holon that can be written, and across stores that answer is never in doubt: a reader's notes, their reading list, their runs and their layout all sit in their own home and point into stores they only read, and as glass is built nothing writes into a pulled store; whether a source may be written is its own to say, as [the store](ref:01M6M9PESE307QYKEJVMRS5T8J) tells. Within one store the side that owns the order holds it: a brief its parts, an album its tracks, a playlist its entries. An entry of something kept by time points at what keeps it instead, since such entries are ordered by a value, the day said or the moment visited, so adding one writes one holon and touches nothing else.

A relation that has a time or attributes of its own is a holon of its own, holding references: a role, who, where, as what, from and to; a run, which program, given what. A visit is one such, when and what one looked at, kept as an entry in the reader's history rather than a holon of its own, as [the interface](ref:01M6JZY20ZJAAP3CBJ4KRDBXFD) tells; whether such entries are holons each is [open](ref:01M6F8G0M0D9XYVG6X8PKDAYE2).

*The author's, 2026-11-02: you can't manipulate someone else's knowledge, but you define your own routes over it; a brief holds its children, a visit belongs instead. The rest found by the simulations.*
body.title: Who holds a relation is who can write
